title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+

citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: Alabama admitted premium tax payment via OPTins

title: IIPRC member-state coverage tracking and compliance maintenance

title: IIPRC single-filing submission via SERFF for eligible products

citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: IIPRC-path eligibility determination for life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: Before initiating any state-by-state filing for life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability products, the insurer must evaluate whether the product qualifies for filing under the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) standards. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)
frequency: per new product or material revision

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Alabama must be submitted electronically via NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. Pass condition: each filing is transmitted through SERFF and accepted by the Alabama Department of Insurance before the product goes live.
citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: SERFF Filing Evidence Preservation (Receipt ID, Status, Submission Date)
requirement: For every Alabama rate, rule, or form filing submitted via SERFF, the filing receipt ID, approval/acknowledgment status, and submission date must be captured and retained before product implementation commences. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: Alabama surplus lines premium tax and data reporting via SLIP+
requirement: For all Alabama surplus lines transactions, the insurer must submit surplus lines tax payments and associated transaction data through the SLIP+ system (not OPTins), as adopted by Alabama to replace OPTins for surplus lines reporting. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: Surplus lines tax remittance via Alabama designated electronic platform
requirement: The insurer must calculate and remit Alabama surplus lines premium taxes through the state-designated electronic platform for each applicable surplus lines transaction. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: Surplus lines transaction data submission via Alabama designated electronic platform
requirement: The insurer must submit complete surplus lines transaction data (policy details, premium, coverage, insured information) to the Alabama state-designated electronic platform for each surplus lines placement. The obligation is met when all required transaction records are successfully uploaded and accepted by the platform without material errors or rejections.
citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: FROI/SROI EDI Acknowledgment Tracking & Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, reconcile, and retain the electronic acknowledgment (999/TA1 or equivalent IAIABC EDI acknowledgment) returned by the Alabama regulator for every FROI/SROI transmission, including evidence of accepted, rejected, and corrected records. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: FROI/SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every covered Alabama workers' compensation claim, the insurer must electronically transmit First Reports of Injury (FROI) and Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the Alabama regulator using IAIABC EDI transaction sets within the prescribed statutory timeframes. citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain an active trading-partner registration with the Alabama workers' compensation regulator (or its designated EDI clearinghouse) under IAIABC EDI standards before transmitting any FROI/SROI data. Pass condition: a current, regulator-acknowledged trading-partner agreement is on file and renewed whenever required.
citation: Alabama Insurance Code (Title 27, Code of Alabama)

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+

title: Electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings via SERFF
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Alaska must be submitted electronically through NAIC SERFF. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted via SERFF prior to product implementation, with no paper or non-SERFF submission pathway used.

title: IIPRC Compact filing eligibility determination

title: IIPRC product filing submission via SERFF Compact portal

title: Preservation of SERFF filing evidence prior to product implementation
requirement: Before any product is implemented in Alaska, the insurer must retain the SERFF filing evidence — including the receipt ID, filing status, and submission date — as a durable record. title: FROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying workplace injury, the insurer must electronically submit a First Report of Injury (FROI) to the Alaska workers' compensation regulator using IAIABC EDI transaction sets within the state-mandated filing deadline. title: FROI/SROI Acknowledgment Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, store, and be able to produce evidence of functional acknowledgments (and any error/rejection responses) received from the Alaska regulator for every FROI and SROI transmission. title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration

title: SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI

title: IIPRC Compact approval record-keeping and ongoing compliance

citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

title: IIPRC-eligible product identification and filing-path selection
requirement: The insurer must assess each new or revised life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product to determine whether it qualifies under IIPRC product standards, and must elect the Compact filing path (via SERFF) for all qualifying products seeking multi-state approval. citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

title: SERFF electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings

title: SERFF filing evidence preservation (receipt ID, status, submission date)

citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the Arizona workers' compensation regulator under IAIABC EDI standards before any FROI/SROI transmissions are made. Pass condition: a current, regulator-confirmed trading-partner agreement/registration record is on file and renewed whenever required.
citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

requirement: The insurer must electronically transmit Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the Arizona workers' compensation regulator using IAIABC EDI standards whenever a reportable status change or update occurs on an open claim. citation: Title 20 of the Arizona Revised Statutes

requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to the Arkansas Insurance Department through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository each year. requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain its Arkansas Certificate of Authority and any corporate changes (e.g., name change, expansion of lines, withdrawal) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). title: Producer/Agent Licensing, Renewal & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must manage all Arkansas producer/agent license applications, renewals, and appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository for distribution to the Arkansas Insurance Department each year. The obligation is met when MCAS data is accurately reported and confirmed as received by the NAIC system and made available to the Arkansas regulator.

title: Electronic premium tax payment via OPTins
requirement: The insurer must submit all Arkansas premium tax payments electronically through the NAIC OPTins system, in accordance with Arkansas's acceptance or requirement of that channel. The obligation is met when each due premium tax payment is transmitted and confirmed via OPTins on or before the applicable statutory due date.

title: IIPRC Compact filing pathway election for eligible life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: For eligible life insurance, annuity, long-term care, and disability products, the insurer must file once through the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) via the SERFF portal rather than filing separately in each member state, including Arkansas. The obligation is satisfied when a single Compact filing is submitted and acknowledged through SERFF, providing uniform approval coverage across all IIPRC member states.

title: SERFF electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Arkansas must be submitted electronically via NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF with a valid submission date recorded before any related product goes live.

title: SERFF filing evidence preservation (receipt ID, status, submission date)
requirement: For every rate, rule, or form filing submitted through SERFF for Arkansas, the filing evidence — including the SERFF receipt ID, current filing status, and submission date — must be captured and retained before product implementation. The pass condition is that a retrievable record of all three data elements exists for each filing at the point of product launch.

title: Surplus lines tax filing and payment via OPTins
requirement: Where Arkansas requires surplus lines tax filings to be submitted electronically, the insurer must use the NAIC OPTins system for both the filing and associated tax payment. The obligation is met when each surplus lines tax filing and its corresponding payment are successfully transmitted through OPTins by the applicable deadline.

title: EDI Transmission Acknowledgment Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, reconcile, and retain acknowledgment records (999/TA1 or equivalent IAIABC EDI acknowledgment transactions) for every FROI/SROI transmission to evidence successful receipt by the Arkansas Workers' Compensation Commission. Pass condition: a complete, auditable acknowledgment log exists for each outbound transaction with no unresolved rejection codes.

title: FROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: The insurer must electronically submit First Reports of Injury (FROI) to the Arkansas Workers' Compensation Commission using IAIABC EDI standards within the state-mandated filing timeframe for each qualifying injury. Pass condition: every reportable FROI is transmitted via compliant EDI transaction sets with no overdue or rejected filings outstanding.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the Arkansas Workers' Compensation Commission (AWCC) EDI system before any FROI/SROI transactions are transmitted. Pass condition: a valid, current trading-partner agreement/registration record is on file with the AWCC and internally documented.

title: SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: The insurer must electronically submit Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the Arkansas Workers' Compensation Commission using IAIABC EDI standards whenever a change in claim status, return-to-work, or closure occurs. Pass condition: every required SROI update is transmitted via compliant EDI transaction sets within applicable deadlines with no overdue or rejected filings outstanding.

title: Annual Independent Cybersecurity Audit Execution
requirement: The insurer must complete an annual independent cybersecurity audit covering the prior calendar year, with the first audit covering 2027 due by April 1, 2028 (for entities with revenue over $100M), and annually thereafter. Pass condition: a completed, independent audit report exists for each covered year within the required timeframe.

title: Cybersecurity Audit Certification Submission to CPPA
requirement: Following completion of the annual independent cybersecurity audit, the insurer must submit a formal certification to the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) on the revenue-phased schedule (first certification by April 1, 2028 for entities over $100M in revenue, annually thereafter). Pass condition: certification is filed with the CPPA by the applicable deadline for each audit year.

title: 45-Day Access Request Response SLA
requirement: The insurer must track every verifiable PI access request from receipt date and ensure a complete response is delivered to the consumer within 45 calendar days, with any permissible extension documented and communicated. The obligation is satisfied when no response exceeds the statutory deadline without a documented extension notice sent within the initial 45-day window.

title: ADMT Appeal & Human Review Pathway
requirement: The insurer must establish and maintain a documented appeal process allowing individuals adversely affected by an ADMT-driven significant decision to request human review and contest the outcome. Pass condition: an appeal procedure exists, is communicated to the individual, appeals are logged, and outcomes are tracked with evidence of genuine human re-evaluation.

title: ADMT GDPR Art. 22 & EU AI Act Crosswalk Documentation
requirement: The insurer must produce and maintain a regulatory crosswalk document mapping each in-scope ADMT use case to the corresponding obligations under GDPR Article 22 (right not to be subject to solely automated decisions) and the EU AI Act (high-risk AI system requirements), identifying gaps and control equivalences. Pass condition: crosswalk is current, reviewed at least annually or upon material change to any ADMT system, and approved by the Data Protection Officer.
frequency: annual or upon material ADMT change

title: ADMT Logic & Outcome Disclosure
requirement: Upon request, the insurer must provide an affected individual with meaningful information about the logic of the ADMT system used in a significant decision and the outcome it produced, including key input factors and their influence. Pass condition: disclosure is provided within the jurisdiction-mandated timeframe, covers the specific decision, and is intelligible to a layperson.

title: ADMT Opt-Out Mechanism
requirement: The insurer must provide data subjects with a functional, accessible mechanism to opt out of ADMT-driven significant decisions (automated underwriting, pricing, claims adjudication) and ensure that opt-out requests are honored by routing the decision to a human reviewer. Pass condition: opt-out requests are processed without detriment to the individual and a human review path is demonstrably available.

title: ADMT Pre-Use Notice Delivery
requirement: Before any Automated Decision-Making Technology (ADMT) substantially replaces human judgment in a significant decision (underwriting, pricing, or claims), the insurer must deliver a clear, plain-language pre-use notice to the affected individual disclosing that ADMT is being used and the nature of its role. Pass condition: notice is delivered prior to the automated decision being rendered, with documented proof of delivery.

title: CCPA 'Business' Threshold Determination
requirement: Meridian must formally assess and document whether it qualifies as a 'business' under CCPA/CPRA by evaluating each applicable threshold (annual gross revenues, volume of personal information bought/sold/shared, or percentage of revenue derived from selling/sharing PI). The obligation is passed when a written threshold analysis is produced, reviewed, and kept current as business conditions change.
frequency: annual, or upon material change in business conditions

title: CCPA In-Scope PI Identification for Non-GLBA Data Subjects
requirement: Meridian must identify and document all categories of personal information that fall outside the GLBA exemption and therefore remain subject to CCPA/CPRA obligations — specifically covering web visitors, prospects, marketing contacts, employees and job applicants, and B2B contacts. The pass condition is a maintained register of these non-GLBA PI categories with their associated data subjects, processing purposes, and applicable CCPA rights mapped to each category.
frequency: annual, or upon material change in data collection or processing

title: Cessation of sale/sharing upon opt-out request
requirement: Upon receipt of a valid consumer opt-out request, the insurer must stop selling or sharing that consumer's personal information — including disclosure for cross-context behavioral advertising — within the timeframe required by CCPA-CPRA (no later than 15 business days). Pass condition: verified halt of all downstream data transfers qualifying as 'sale' or 'sharing' for the requesting consumer within the statutory deadline.

title: Consumer PI Access Response – Categories & Specific Pieces
requirement: Upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request, the insurer must disclose the specific categories and specific pieces of personal information (PI) collected about the consumer, covering at least the prior 12 months. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, accurate disclosure is delivered to the verified requestor within 45 days of receipt of the request.

title: Consumer PI Access Response – Sources & Business Purposes
requirement: Upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request, the insurer must disclose the sources from which PI was collected and the business or commercial purposes for which it was collected or used, covering at least the prior 12 months. The obligation is satisfied when this disclosure is delivered to the verified requestor within 45 days of receipt of the request.

title: Consumer PI Access Response – Third-Party Recipients
requirement: Upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request, the insurer must disclose the categories of third parties with whom the consumer's PI was shared or sold, covering at least the prior 12 months. The obligation is satisfied when this disclosure is delivered to the verified requestor within 45 days of receipt of the request.

title: Consumer PI deletion execution on verifiable request
requirement: Upon receipt of a verified consumer deletion request, the insurer must locate and delete all personal information (PI) held about that consumer from its own systems and records, subject to statutory exceptions (e.g., legal hold, regulatory retention mandates). The obligation is satisfied when PI is confirmed deleted or suppressed across all internal repositories within the timeframe required by applicable law.

title: Consumer Request Acknowledgement Within 10 Business Days
requirement: Upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request, the insurer must send a written acknowledgement to the requester within 10 business days confirming receipt and outlining how the request will be processed. Pass condition: 100% of requests have a timestamped acknowledgement issued within 10 business days of receipt.

title: Consumer Request Identity Verification
requirement: Before processing any consumer data privacy request, the insurer must verify the identity of the requester using a reasonable and documented verification process appropriate to the sensitivity of the request. Pass condition: a written identity verification procedure exists, is consistently applied to all incoming requests, and verification outcomes are logged.

title: Consumer Request Records Retention (24-Month Minimum)
requirement: The organization must maintain a complete record of every consumer privacy request received (e.g., access, deletion, correction, opt-out) and the specific handling actions taken for each, retained for a minimum of 24 months from the date of the request. Pass condition: records are retrievable for any request made within the prior 24 months and include request type, receipt date, response actions, and outcome.

title: Consumer Request Response Within 45-Day Deadline
requirement: The insurer must substantively respond to a verified consumer data privacy request within 45 calendar days of receipt, including all required disclosures; if additional time is needed, the deadline may be extended once by up to an additional 45 calendar days with prior consumer notification stating the reason for the extension. Pass condition: all responses are delivered within the initial 45-day window or within the extended 90-day total window with documented consumer notification of the extension.

title: Cross-context behavioral advertising disclosure controls
requirement: The insurer must identify all data flows in which consumer personal information is disclosed to third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising and treat each such disclosure as 'sharing' subject to opt-out rights under CCPA-CPRA. Pass condition: a documented data-flow inventory exists mapping all behavioral-advertising disclosures, and contractual and technical controls are in place to suppress those flows for opted-out consumers.

title: Do Not Sell or Share opt-out mechanism
requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain a clear, accessible 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link or equivalent mechanism (e.g., on its website and any consumer-facing digital properties) that allows California consumers to submit an opt-out request. Pass condition: the mechanism is present, functional, and clearly labeled at all times without requiring account creation or undue burden.

title: Downstream deletion directive to service providers and contractors
requirement: Upon executing a consumer PI deletion, the insurer must notify and instruct all service providers and contractors that have received the consumer's PI to delete it from their own systems, subject to statutory exceptions. The obligation is satisfied when documented deletion directives have been issued to each relevant third party and confirmation of deletion is obtained and recorded.

title: Dual Consumer Request Method Provision
requirement: The insurer must offer at least two distinct methods (e.g., toll-free number and web form) through which consumers can submit data privacy requests. Pass condition: at minimum two functional, documented submission channels are available and accessible to consumers at all times.

title: Financial Incentive Program Disclosure Notice
requirement: Before enrolling a consumer in any financial incentive or price/service difference program tied to personal data, the insurer must provide a clear and conspicuous notice disclosing the material terms of the program, including the categories of data collected, the value of the data, and the consumer's right to withdraw at any time. Pass condition: a compliant notice is presented and recorded prior to enrollment for every such program.

title: Financial Incentive Program Permissibility & Reasonableness Standard
requirement: Any financial incentive, price difference, or service difference offered in exchange for consumer data must be reasonably related to the value of the data provided by the consumer and must not be unjust, unreasonable, or coercive. Pass condition: a documented valuation analysis is maintained that quantifies the estimated value of consumer data and confirms each incentive offering is proportionate to that value.

title: GLBA Exemption Scope Mapping for Personal Information
requirement: Meridian must conduct an information-level analysis to identify which categories of personal information are exempt from CCPA obligations because they are collected and used subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (e.g., nonpublic personal financial information of insurance policyholders). The analysis must produce a documented data inventory that labels each PI category as 'GLBA-exempt' or 'CCPA in-scope,' and must be updated whenever new data types or processing activities are introduced.
frequency: annual, or upon introduction of new data types/processing activities

title: GPC Opt-Out Honoring — Sale/Sharing Suppression
requirement: Upon detection of a valid GPC or equivalent opt-out preference signal, the insurer must immediately treat it as a binding opt-out of sale and sharing of the consumer's personal information and suppress all downstream sale/sharing processing for that individual. Pass condition: no personal data of a GPC-signaling consumer is sold or shared from the moment the signal is detected onward.

title: GPC Signal Detection Mechanism
requirement: The insurer must implement technical capability to automatically detect browser/device opt-out preference signals (e.g., Global Privacy Control) at every consumer-facing digital touchpoint. Pass condition: every inbound GPC or equivalent signal is reliably captured and logged without requiring manual consumer action.

title: Heightened Safeguards for Financial & Precise-Geolocation SPI
requirement: Apply enhanced administrative, technical, and physical safeguards — including strict access controls, encryption, and retention limits — to financial account data and precise-geolocation data collected or derived during insurance operations (e.g., telematics, premium billing). Pass condition: a documented, tested control framework for financial and geolocation SPI exists, with access logs confirming least-privilege enforcement.

title: Heightened Safeguards for Health & Biometric SPI
requirement: Apply enhanced administrative, technical, and physical safeguards (e.g., encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access, minimization, and purpose-binding) specifically to health and biometric data processed in insurance underwriting, claims, and operations. Pass condition: a documented control set exists for health/biometric SPI that exceeds baseline PII controls, with evidence of implementation and testing.

title: Incompatible-Purpose Notice Requirement
requirement: Before using or disclosing personal information for a purpose that is materially incompatible with the purpose originally disclosed to the consumer, the insurer must provide conspicuous advance notice (and obtain any required consent) to the affected consumer. Pass condition: a documented process exists that identifies incompatible secondary uses, triggers a consumer notice workflow prior to such use, and retains evidence of notice delivery.

title: Large Processor Consumer Request Metrics Disclosure
requirement: Organizations meeting the regulatory threshold for 'large processor' must compile aggregate metrics on consumer privacy requests (e.g., number received by type, median response times, denial rates) and disclose these metrics to the regulator or publicly as required. Pass condition: a complete metrics report covering the applicable reporting period is compiled and submitted/published within the required deadline.

title: Minor (Ages 13–15) Self Opt-In Consent for PI Sale or Sharing
requirement: Before selling or sharing the personal information of consumers aged 13–15, the insurer must obtain affirmative opt-in consent directly from the minor consumer themselves. The pass condition is that no PI of any 13-to-15-year-old consumer is sold or shared without a documented opt-in recorded from that consumer.

title: Non-Discrimination Prohibition for Rights Exercisers
requirement: The insurer must not deny, charge different prices for, or provide a different level or quality of goods/services to any consumer solely because they exercised a data privacy right (e.g., access, deletion, opt-out). Pass condition: documented operational controls and monitoring demonstrate that no adverse treatment is applied to consumers who have exercised a privacy right.

title: Nonencrypted/Nonredacted PI Breach — Private Right of Action Liability Controls
requirement: The insurer must ensure that all PI at rest and in transit is encrypted or redacted to eliminate statutory exposure to the CCPA private right of action ($100–$750 per consumer per incident). Pass condition: no nonencrypted and nonredacted PI is accessible in a breach scenario, verified by encryption coverage assessments and penetration testing results.

title: Notice at Collection – Categories & Purposes Disclosure
requirement: At or before the point of personal information (PI) and sensitive personal information (SPI) collection, the insurer must present a clear disclosure naming every category of PI/SPI being collected and the specific business purpose(s) for which each category is used. The obligation is met when a compliant notice is demonstrably delivered to the data subject prior to or at the moment of collection, covering all active collection channels (web, paper, call center, etc.).

title: Notice at Collection – Retention Period Disclosure
requirement: At or before collection of any PI or SPI, the insurer must disclose the retention period (or the criteria used to determine it) for each category of personal information collected. The obligation is satisfied when all collection-point notices include a retention schedule or a clear criteria-based retention statement aligned to the insurer's approved data retention policy.

title: Notice at Collection – Sale or Sharing Disclosure
requirement: At or before collection of PI or SPI, the insurer must disclose whether any category of PI or SPI is sold to third parties or shared with third parties for cross-context behavioral advertising or other purposes. The obligation is met when all active collection-point notices explicitly state, per category, whether a sale or sharing arrangement exists, including a 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link where applicable.

title: PI Collection Minimization Standard
requirement: The insurer must define and document, for each data collection point, a specific business purpose and collect only the personal information that is reasonably necessary and proportionate to that disclosed purpose. Pass condition: a documented data inventory exists mapping every PI field collected to a justified, proportionate business purpose with no excess fields collected.

title: PI Retention Schedule Proportionality
requirement: The insurer must establish and enforce a retention schedule that limits the retention of personal information to no longer than is reasonably necessary to fulfill each disclosed purpose, with defined disposal procedures upon expiry. Pass condition: a current, approved retention schedule exists per PI category, automated or procedural disposal is triggered at schedule expiry, and periodic audits confirm no over-retained PI.

title: PI Third-Party Sharing Purpose Limitation
requirement: The insurer must ensure that personal information shared with third parties (vendors, partners, affiliates) is limited to what is reasonably necessary for the disclosed purpose, governed by contractual data-use restrictions aligned to that purpose. Pass condition: all active data-sharing agreements contain purpose-limitation clauses, and a third-party data-sharing register confirms each sharing activity maps to a disclosed consumer purpose.

title: PI Use & Processing Purpose Limitation Control
requirement: The insurer must restrict internal use and processing of personal information strictly to the purposes disclosed to the consumer at or before collection; systems and process controls must prevent use for purposes materially different from those disclosed. Pass condition: documented use-case approvals and technical controls (e.g., data access tagging, query governance) demonstrably block unauthorized internal processing purposes.

title: Parental/Guardian Opt-In Consent for Under-13 PI Sale or Sharing
requirement: Before selling or sharing the personal information of consumers under age 13, the insurer must obtain affirmative opt-in consent from the child's parent or legal guardian. The pass condition is that no PI of any sub-13 consumer is sold or shared without a documented, verifiable parental/guardian opt-in on file.

title: Personal Information Correction on Verified Request
requirement: Upon receipt of a verifiable consumer request, the insurer must correct inaccurate personal information in its systems using commercially reasonable efforts. The obligation is satisfied when the correction is applied and the consumer is notified of the completed update within the timeframe required by applicable law.

title: Personal Information Inventory
requirement: Maintain a complete, up-to-date inventory of all personal information (PI) collected, processed, stored, or shared by the organization, identifying data elements, data flows, sources, and systems of record. The inventory must be documented, version-controlled, and reviewable by compliance personnel at any time.

title: Pre-Processing Privacy Risk Assessment – Written Documentation
requirement: Before initiating any high-risk processing activity (selling or sharing personal information, processing sensitive personal information, using ADMT for significant decisions, training ADMT models, or automated inference of sensitive traits), the insurer must conduct and document a written privacy risk assessment that identifies and evaluates the risks to consumers. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, written risk assessment exists on file prior to commencement of each qualifying high-risk processing activity.

title: Privacy Policy – Annual Review & Update Cycle
requirement: The insurer must review and, where necessary, update the privacy policy at least once every 12 months to ensure ongoing accuracy. The review must be documented and any material changes published before the anniversary date to satisfy the cadence requirement.

title: Privacy Policy – Comprehensive Content Maintenance
requirement: The insurer must maintain a publicly accessible, comprehensive privacy policy that describes consumer rights, categories of personal information collected, purposes of collection and use, and third-party disclosure practices. The policy must be accurate, complete, and reflective of current data processing activities at all times.

title: Privacy Risk Assessment Submission to CPPA
requirement: From April 1, 2028, the insurer must submit the documented privacy risk assessments for all qualifying high-risk processing activities to the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) in the form and manner required by the Agency. The obligation is satisfied when each required assessment has been filed with and acknowledged by the CPPA on or before the applicable submission deadline.
frequency: per high-risk processing activity, from April 1, 2028

title: Reasonable Security Program for Personal Information
requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain documented security procedures and practices that are appropriate to the nature and sensitivity of the personal information (PI) it holds, processes, or transmits. Pass condition: a current, written security program exists, is risk-calibrated to the PI inventory, and is evidenced by periodic review and update.

title: Retention Enforcement & Deletion of PI/SPI Beyond Disclosed Period
requirement: The insurer must operationally enforce data retention schedules by purging or de-identifying each category of PI and SPI once the disclosed retention period expires or the collection purpose is fulfilled, ensuring data is not retained longer than reasonably necessary. The pass condition is that automated or auditable deletion/de-identification controls exist for every PI/SPI category and evidence of timely purge execution is maintained.

title: Retention Period Disclosure by PI/SPI Category
requirement: The insurer must publicly disclose, in its privacy notice, the specific retention period (or the criteria used to determine it) for each category of Personal Information (PI) and Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) it collects. The pass condition is that every PI/SPI category in the data inventory has a corresponding, consumer-facing retention period or determination criteria documented and published.

title: SPI Inventory & Classification
requirement: Maintain a current, documented inventory that identifies and classifies all Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) — including health, biometric, financial, and precise-geolocation data — held or processed across the insurer's systems. Pass condition: a complete SPI data map exists, is reviewed at least annually, and covers all lines of business and data flows.

title: SPI Limit-Use Request Honoring Mechanism
requirement: Implement and operate a consumer-facing mechanism that receives, logs, and fulfills requests to limit the use and disclosure of SPI, ensuring secondary uses cease within the timeframe required by applicable law. Pass condition: all limit-use requests are acknowledged and actioned within the statutory deadline with no unauthorized secondary processing continuing post-request.

title: SPI Secondary-Use Restriction Controls
requirement: Establish and enforce technical and procedural controls that prevent SPI from being used for purposes beyond those disclosed at collection or permitted by law (e.g., cross-context behavioral advertising, sale, or non-essential analytics). Pass condition: documented access controls, data-use agreements, and audit logs demonstrate SPI is not processed for restricted secondary purposes.

title: Sensitive PI Limitation Request Mechanism
requirement: Deploy and maintain a conspicuous 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' mechanism (e.g., a web form, in-app toggle, or toll-free number) through which consumers can submit a restriction request. The pass condition is that the mechanism is live, functional, and accessible to all consumers at all times.

title: Sensitive PI Use Restriction to Necessary Purposes
requirement: Restrict all internal processing, sharing, and use of consumers' Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) solely to what is necessary to perform the specific goods or services requested by the consumer, and honor limitation requests received through the mechanism. The pass condition is that no SPI is used for secondary purposes (e.g., cross-context behavioral advertising, profiling) once a limitation request is received and validated.

title: Sensitive Personal Information Classification Schema
requirement: Define and apply a formal classification schema that identifies and tags sensitive PI categories — including SSNs/government IDs, financial credentials, precise geolocation, health/medical data, biometric data, and sexual orientation — across all data assets in the PI inventory. Pass condition: every data asset in the inventory carries an accurate sensitivity classification label that can be used to scope downstream notice, opt-out, limit-use, security, and retention controls.

title: Third-Party Data Processing Agreement – Compliance Verification / Audit Right Clause
requirement: Every contract with a service provider, contractor, or third party must grant the insurer the right to monitor, audit, or otherwise verify the counterparty's compliance with contractual data-protection obligations. The pass condition is that all applicable contracts include a compliance-verification or audit-right provision that is exercisable on demand or at defined intervals.
frequency: per contract execution; audit rights exercised at minimum annual

title: Third-Party Data Processing Agreement – Deletion & Flow-Down Obligation Clause
requirement: Every contract with a service provider, contractor, or third party must require the counterparty to delete personal information upon termination or request and to flow down equivalent obligations to any sub-processors or subcontractors. The pass condition is that all applicable contracts include enforceable deletion and sub-processor flow-down clauses.

title: Third-Party Data Processing Agreement – Purpose Limitation Clause
requirement: Every contract with a service provider, contractor, or third party that processes personal information must include an explicit clause restricting data use to the specified, documented purposes only. The pass condition is that 100% of applicable contracts contain a purpose-limitation provision that is reviewed and executed prior to any data sharing.

title: Third-Party Data Processing Agreement – Sale/Disclosure Prohibition Clause
requirement: Every contract with a service provider, contractor, or third party must include an express prohibition on the unauthorized sale, sharing, or further disclosure of personal information received under the agreement. The pass condition is that all applicable contracts contain a binding anti-sale/anti-disclosure provision before data transfer commences.

title: Verifiable Consumer Request Authentication Mechanism
requirement: The insurer must maintain a documented process to authenticate and verify the identity of consumers submitting PI access requests before any disclosure is made. The obligation is satisfied when every access request is gated through a repeatable verification procedure that prevents unauthorized disclosure.

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to the California Department of Insurance through the NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is satisfied when the complete statutory financial statement is successfully filed via iSite+ and distributed to the state regulator within the required filing deadline.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Changes via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file and maintain its California Certificate of Authority and submit all qualifying corporate changes (e.g., name, domicile, lines of business) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is met when the company's California authority is current and any reportable corporate change is submitted via UCAA prior to or concurrent with the effective date of the change.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must ensure all California producers/agents hold valid licenses, renewals, and appointments processed through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is met when every active producer/agent writing California business has a current, NIPR-filed license and appointment on record with no lapses.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the California Department of Insurance through the NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is satisfied when all required MCAS data elements are accurately reported, successfully transmitted via iSite+, and distributed to the state regulator by the applicable deadline.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: The insurer must submit all California rate, rule, and form filings electronically via NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF with a valid submission date, confirming the electronic submission channel requirement is met.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: SERFF Filing Evidence Preservation (Receipt ID, Status, Submission Date)
requirement: The insurer must capture and retain the SERFF receipt ID, filing status, and submission date for every rate, rule, and form filing before any associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that a complete filing evidence record is retrievable in the document/records system for each SERFF submission prior to product launch.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Separate California direct filing for Compact-eligible LTC products
requirement: Because California is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, long-term care insurance products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the California Department of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, standalone California state filing for each LTC product is submitted and approved prior to sale in the state.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Separate California direct filing for Compact-eligible annuity products
requirement: Because California is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, annuity products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the California Department of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, standalone California state filing for each annuity product is submitted and approved prior to sale in the state.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Separate California direct filing for Compact-eligible disability products
requirement: Because California is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, disability insurance products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the California Department of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, standalone California state filing for each disability product is submitted and approved prior to sale in the state.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Separate California direct filing for Compact-eligible life products
requirement: Because California is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, life insurance products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the California Department of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, standalone California state filing for each life product is submitted and approved prior to sale in the state.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Electronic FROI/SROI transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying workers' compensation claim, the insurer must electronically submit First Reports of Injury (FROI) and Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the California regulator in compliance with current IAIABC EDI transaction-set specifications and required data elements. Pass condition: each reportable claim event triggers a timely, well-formed EDI transaction submitted within the mandated timeframe with no fatal-error rejections.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: FROI/SROI acknowledgment evidence retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, store, and be able to produce regulator-issued EDI acknowledgment records (e.g., 999/TA1 functional acknowledgments and loop-level error reports) for every FROI/SROI transmission as evidence of successful receipt and acceptance. Pass condition: acknowledgment artifacts for all submitted transactions are retained and retrievable for audit or examination on demand.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: IAIABC EDI trading-partner registration for FROI/SROI
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain an active trading-partner registration with the California workers' compensation regulator (WCIRB/DIR) under IAIABC EDI standards before transmitting any FROI or SROI transactions. Pass condition: a current, regulator-acknowledged trading-partner agreement/enrollment record is on file and has not lapsed.
citation: Title 10, Chapter 5 of the California Code of Regulations

title: Colorado APCD recurring claims data extract submission
requirement: Health insurers must prepare and submit recurring claims data extracts to the Colorado All-Payer Claims Database in accordance with the state's APCD submission guide. The obligation is satisfied when complete, valid extract files are delivered to the Colorado APCD on each required submission cycle without material errors or rejections.

title: Real-time DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer must maintain the technical capability to receive and respond to individual motor vehicle insurance verification queries initiated by the Colorado DMV or state verification program, returning accurate coverage status in the required electronic format within mandated response timeframes. The obligation is met when the system is continuously available, all inbound queries receive a timely and accurate response, and no unresolved query failures are outstanding.

title: Recurring policy data feed to Colorado motor vehicle insurance verification program
requirement: The insurer must establish and maintain automated, recurring electronic data feeds from its policy administration systems to the Colorado motor vehicle insurance verification program, delivering current auto policy data (policy number, insured, vehicle, effective/expiration dates) on the required cadence. The obligation is met when feeds are transmitted on schedule, data is accurate and complete, and the state/DMV confirms successful receipt without material errors.

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to Colorado through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository, which distributes the filing to the Colorado Division of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when the complete annual financial statement is accepted by iSite+ and made available to the state regulator within the required filing deadline.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Changes via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain its Colorado Certificate of Authority and any material corporate changes (e.g., name change, merger, new lines of authority) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). Pass condition: all company licensing actions and corporate changes are filed and approved through UCAA prior to transacting the affected business in Colorado.

title: Producer/Agent Licensing, Renewal & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must ensure all producers, agents, and appointees operating in Colorado are licensed, renewed, and appointed through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). Pass condition: all active Colorado producers have current, NIPR-processed licenses and appointments with no lapsed or unappointed agents transacting business.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to Colorado through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository, which distributes the data to the Colorado Division of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when complete and accurate MCAS data is accepted by iSite+ and made available to the state regulator within the required filing deadline.

title: Electronic premium tax payment submission via OPTins
requirement: The insurer must remit Colorado state premium tax payments electronically through NAIC's OPTins system, as required by the Colorado Division of Insurance. The obligation is satisfied when each premium tax payment is successfully transmitted and confirmed via OPTins by the applicable due date.
frequency: per premium tax due date (typically quarterly/annual)

title: IIPRC SERFF portal filing for eligible life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: For eligible life insurance, annuity, long-term care, and disability income products intended for sale in Colorado and other IIPRC member states, the insurer must file those products through the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) via the SERFF portal as a single multi-state filing rather than individual state filings. The obligation is satisfied when a complete IIPRC filing is submitted through SERFF and approved by the Compact for all targeted member states, including Colorado.

title: SERFF electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings intended for the Colorado market must be submitted electronically via the NAIC SERFF system prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF and accepted by the Colorado Division of Insurance before the product is placed in market.

title: SERFF filing evidence retention (receipt ID, status, submission date)
requirement: For every Colorado rate, rule, or form filing submitted via SERFF, the insurer must preserve the SERFF receipt ID, filing status, and submission date as documentary evidence before the associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that a retrievable record containing all three data elements exists in the document/filing repository for each filed item prior to product launch.

title: Surplus lines tax filing via OPTins (Colorado)
requirement: Where applicable, the insurer must submit Colorado surplus lines tax filings electronically through NAIC's OPTins system. The obligation is met when each surplus lines tax filing is successfully transmitted and acknowledged in OPTins within the state-mandated filing period.
frequency: per surplus lines tax filing due date

title: EDI Transmission Acknowledgment Monitoring & Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, review, and retain acknowledgment responses (999/TA1 or equivalent IAIABC EDI acknowledgment transactions) for every FROI/SROI transmission to confirm acceptance or identify and remediate rejections. Pass condition: acknowledgment evidence for all transmissions is retained per record-retention schedules and any rejected transactions are corrected and resubmitted within the regulator's required cure period.

title: Electronic FROI Submission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying workplace injury in Colorado, the insurer must electronically transmit a First Report of Injury (FROI) transaction set to the Colorado regulator using IAIABC EDI-compliant formats within the state-mandated filing deadline. Pass condition: each FROI is successfully transmitted and the EDI transaction record confirms format compliance with IAIABC release specifications.

title: Electronic SROI Submission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every subsequent change in claim status (e.g., return to work, disability changes, claim closure) on a Colorado workers' comp claim, the insurer must electronically transmit a Subsequent Report of Injury (SROI) transaction set using IAIABC EDI-compliant formats within required timeframes. Pass condition: each SROI is transmitted on time and the EDI record confirms format compliance with IAIABC release specifications.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the Colorado workers' compensation regulator under IAIABC EDI standards before any FROI/SROI transmissions are made. Pass condition: a current, approved trading-partner agreement/registration is on file with the Colorado Division of Workers' Compensation and renewed whenever credentials or connectivity change.

title: Connecticut APCD recurring claims data extract submission
requirement: Health insurers must prepare and submit recurring claims data extracts to Connecticut's all-payer claims database (APCD) in accordance with the state's APCD submission guide, including all required data elements, file formats, and submission schedules. The obligation is satisfied when complete, conforming extracts are delivered to the APCD within each prescribed submission cycle without material errors or rejections.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Real-time DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer's policy administration systems must maintain electronic connectivity to respond to on-demand insurance verification queries initiated by the Connecticut DMV or state verification program. Pass condition: query responses are returned accurately and within required response time thresholds for all in-force auto policies.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Recurring policy data feed to CT motor vehicle insurance verification program
requirement: The insurer's policy administration systems must generate and transmit recurring electronic policy data feeds to Connecticut's motor vehicle insurance verification program, covering all active auto policies. Pass condition: feeds are transmitted on schedule, are complete, and accepted without material error by the state/DMV system.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Annual Financial Statement Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its complete annual financial statement to the Connecticut Insurance Department through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when the annual statement is successfully filed within iSite+ and distributed to the Connecticut regulator by the applicable statutory deadline.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Insurer Company License Application & Corporate Changes via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file for a Certificate of Authority to operate in Connecticut, and submit any material corporate changes (e.g., name change, merger, expansion of lines), using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is satisfied when all required UCAA filings are submitted and approved before the insurer transacts business or implements corporate changes in Connecticut.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes
frequency: per triggering corporate event or new state entry

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain all producer/agent license applications, renewals, and appointment filings in Connecticut through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is satisfied when all active producers transacting business in Connecticut hold current, NIPR-filed licenses and appointments in good standing.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes
frequency: continuous, with renewal per license expiration cycle

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) Data Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the Connecticut Insurance Department through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when complete and accurate MCAS data is successfully filed within iSite+ and distributed to the Connecticut regulator by the applicable deadline.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: IIPRC Compact Filing Eligibility Determination
requirement: The insurer must assess each life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability product to determine whether it qualifies for filing through the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) rather than individual state filings. Pass condition: a documented eligibility assessment exists for every in-scope product prior to filing, confirming Compact eligibility or state-level filing rationale.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: IIPRC Compact Filing Maintenance & Amendment Management
requirement: The insurer must maintain all active IIPRC Compact-filed products in good standing, submitting amendments through the SERFF portal whenever product forms, rates, or riders are revised, ensuring continuous Compact-approval coverage across all member states. Pass condition: no Compact-filed product is marketed or issued using forms or rates that differ from the current approved Compact filing without a corresponding amendment on file.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: IIPRC Compact Product Submission via SERFF
requirement: For all eligible life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability products, the insurer must submit a single Compact filing through the SERFF portal to the IIPRC, covering all member states including Connecticut, in lieu of separate state filings. Pass condition: eligible products have an active, accepted IIPRC filing in SERFF with a Compact approval on record before the product is marketed or issued in any member state.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Preservation of SERFF Filing Evidence Prior to Product Implementation
requirement: For each Connecticut rate, rule, or form filing submitted via SERFF, the insurer must retain and store the filing evidence — including receipt ID, filing status, and submission date — before the associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that all three data elements are recorded and retrievable in the filing record system prior to any product launch activity.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Connecticut must be submitted electronically through the NAIC SERFF system prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted via SERFF and a valid receipt ID and submission date are generated by the system.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Connecticut Workers' Comp Claim Reporting Channel & Format Compliance
requirement: The insurer must identify, document, and operationalize Connecticut's mixed/non-EDI emphasis reporting channel and format requirements for workers' compensation claims, ensuring that claim data is submitted to the Connecticut Workers' Compensation Commission via the state-prescribed mix of electronic and non-electronic methods. Pass condition: all required CT workers' comp claim reports are submitted through the correct channel(s) and in the correct format(s) as specified by Connecticut statute and regulation, with no use of a non-approved EDI-only submission path.
citation: Title 38a of the Connecticut General Statutes

title: Annual Financial Statement Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to Delaware's regulator through the NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository each year. The obligation is satisfied when a complete, timely annual statement is accepted by iSite+ and distributed to the Delaware Department of Insurance.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Change Filing via UCAA (Delaware)
requirement: The insurer must obtain and maintain its Delaware Certificate of Authority, and submit any corporate changes (e.g., name, domicile, lines of business) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). Pass condition: all active company authority is reflected in a current UCAA filing accepted by the Delaware DOI, with no unlicensed operations or unfiiled corporate changes.
frequency: per corporate change or renewal cycle

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment Maintenance via NIPR (Delaware)
requirement: The insurer must ensure all producers/agents transacting business in Delaware are licensed, renewed, and appointed through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). Pass condition: all active Delaware producers have current, NIPR-processed licenses and appointments with no lapsed or unauthorized producers writing business in the state.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to Delaware's regulator through the NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository each year. The obligation is satisfied when the MCAS data file is accepted by iSite+ and made available to the Delaware Department of Insurance for market conduct oversight purposes.

title: IIPRC filing inventory and compliance tracking
requirement: The insurer must maintain an up-to-date inventory of all products filed and approved through the IIPRC Compact, including filing dates, approval status, member-state coverage, and any post-approval amendments. Pass condition: the inventory is current, reconciled against SERFF records, and available for regulatory examination on demand.

title: IIPRC uniform product filing submission via SERFF
requirement: For all IIPRC-eligible life, annuity, LTC, and disability products, the insurer must submit a complete filing through the Compact's SERFF portal using IIPRC uniform standards, covering all member states in a single filing event. Pass condition: the SERFF filing is accepted and assigned an IIPRC transaction number prior to state-level market deployment.

title: IIPRC-eligible product identification and filing-path selection
requirement: The insurer must evaluate each new or revised life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product to determine whether it meets IIPRC eligibility criteria, and must affirmatively select the Compact filing path (via SERFF) when eligibility is confirmed. Pass condition: a documented eligibility determination exists for every in-scope product prior to filing submission.

title: Pre-Implementation Preservation of SERFF Filing Evidence
requirement: Prior to any product implementation in Delaware, the insurer must capture and retain the SERFF receipt ID, filing status, and submission date for each rate, rule, or form filing. A filing record is compliant only when all three evidence elements are documented and stored before the product goes live.

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings destined for Delaware must be submitted electronically through NAIC SERFF. A filing is compliant only when each submission is routed via SERFF (not paper or alternative channels) and confirmed as received by the Delaware Department of Insurance.

title: EDI Acknowledgment Receipt & Error Resolution Evidence
requirement: The insurer must capture, retain, and act upon acknowledgment transactions (e.g., TA1, 999, or regulator-issued acceptance/rejection responses) returned by the Delaware EDI system for every FROI/SROI submission, resolving any rejected transactions within the required cure period. Pass condition: a complete, auditable log of acknowledgments exists for all transmissions, with documented evidence that rejections were corrected and resubmitted.

title: FROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying first report of injury in Delaware, the insurer must electronically transmit a compliant First Report of Injury (FROI) transaction set to the Delaware workers' compensation regulator using IAIABC EDI standards within the state-mandated timeframe. Pass condition: each FROI is transmitted on time and formatted in conformance with the applicable IAIABC EDI release.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain an active trading-partner registration with Delaware's workers' compensation EDI system before transmitting any FROI/SROI transactions. Pass condition: a current, accepted trading-partner agreement/registration record is on file with the Delaware WC regulator.

title: SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying subsequent change in claim status in Delaware, the insurer must electronically transmit a compliant Subsequent Report of Injury (SROI) transaction set to the Delaware workers' compensation regulator using IAIABC EDI standards within the state-mandated timeframe. Pass condition: each SROI is transmitted on time and formatted in conformance with the applicable IAIABC EDI release.

title: Real-time DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer must maintain a system capability to receive and respond to on-demand electronic insurance verification queries from the DC DMV or its designated verification system. Pass condition: the insurer's policy administration or integration layer returns accurate, timely coverage status responses to all inbound state/DMV queries within the timeframe mandated by the program.

title: Recurring policy data feed to DC motor vehicle insurance verification program
requirement: The insurer must configure policy administration systems to generate and transmit recurring electronic policy data feeds to the District of Columbia's motor vehicle insurance verification program. Pass condition: feeds are delivered at the required cadence, contain all mandated policy fields, and are accepted without rejection errors by the DC/DMV system.

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement (Annual Statement blank) to the District of Columbia regulator through NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when the filing is accepted by iSite+ and distributed to the DC regulator within the statutory deadline.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Change Filing via UCAA (DC)
requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain its certificate of authority in the District of Columbia — including any corporate changes (e.g., name changes, mergers, new lines of business) — using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is met when the company holds a current, valid DC certificate of authority reflecting all approved corporate changes, filed and approved through the UCAA portal.
frequency: event-driven (per corporate change) and continuous (certificate maintenance)

title: Producer/Agent Licensing, Renewal & Appointment via NIPR (DC)
requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain all producer/agent license applications, renewals, and appointments in the District of Columbia through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is met when all active DC producers and agents hold a current, NIPR-filed license and appointment in good standing, with no unlicensed individuals transacting insurance business.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the District of Columbia regulator through NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when the MCAS data is accepted and distributed to the DC regulator by the required deadline, with all required data elements accurately reported.

title: IIPRC compact filing submission via SERFF portal
requirement: Eligible life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability product forms and rates must be filed once through the Compact's SERFF portal covering all IIPRC member states (including DC) rather than filed separately in each state. Pass condition: the filing record in SERFF reflects a Compact multi-state submission with DC jurisdiction included and an acknowledgment or approval from the IIPRC Product Standards Office.

title: IIPRC filing currency and ongoing compliance maintenance
requirement: The insurer must monitor IIPRC product standards for updates and maintain all Compact-approved forms in continuing compliance with current standards, filing amendments through the SERFF portal whenever standards change or the product is revised. Pass condition: no Compact-approved form remains in use after an applicable IIPRC standard revision deadline without a conforming amendment filing on record.

title: IIPRC-eligible product identification and filing-path election
requirement: For each life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product intended for DC and other member states, the insurer must assess eligibility under IIPRC standards and formally elect the Compact filing path where eligible, documenting the eligibility determination before submission. Pass condition: a written eligibility assessment and filing-path election decision exists for every in-scope product prior to any regulatory submission.

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for the District of Columbia must be submitted electronically via the NAIC SERFF system. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF (not by paper or alternate channel) and accepted by the DC Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking prior to product implementation.

title: SERFF Filing Evidence Preservation (Receipt ID, Status, Submission Date)
requirement: For every DC rate, rule, or form filing submitted via SERFF, the insurer must capture and retain the filing receipt ID, current approval status, and submission date before any associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that these three data points are recorded in a durable filing repository and retrievable for audit prior to product launch.

title: EDI Transmission Acknowledgment Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, store, and be able to produce evidence of acknowledgment (999/TA1 or equivalent IAIABC EDI acknowledgment transactions) for every FROI and SROI transmission sent to the DC regulator. Pass condition: a retrievable acknowledgment record exists for each submitted transaction demonstrating regulator receipt and acceptance status.

title: FROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying workers' compensation injury occurring in the District of Columbia, the insurer must submit a First Report of Injury (FROI) electronically to the DC regulator in compliance with IAIABC EDI format and timing requirements. Pass condition: each FROI is transmitted within the jurisdictionally mandated timeframe and conforms to current IAIABC EDI transaction set specifications.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the District of Columbia's workers' compensation regulator under IAIABC EDI standards before any FROI/SROI transmissions may occur. Pass condition: a current, regulator-confirmed trading-partner agreement and registration record is on file.

title: SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every open DC workers' compensation claim requiring a status update, the insurer must submit Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) electronically to the DC regulator in IAIABC EDI format at each required lifecycle event or interval. Pass condition: all SROIs are transmitted on time and pass IAIABC EDI validation without rejection.

title: 72-Hour Supervisory Authority Breach Notification
requirement: Upon detection of a personal data breach, the insurer must assess it and, where required, notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware. The pass condition is a documented, timestamped notification to the regulator delivered within the 72-hour window for all qualifying breach events.

title: Absolute direct-marketing opt-out enforcement
requirement: The organization must implement an absolute, unconditional opt-out mechanism for direct marketing such that, once a data subject exercises this right, all marketing communications and profiling for direct-marketing purposes are halted across every channel and downstream campaign job. The pass condition is that no direct-marketing material is sent and no marketing profile is built or used for that individual after opt-out is recorded.

title: Art. 9(2) Legal Basis Documentation for Special-Category Data
requirement: For every processing activity involving health, biometric, genetic, or other special-category data (including medical evidence in claims and underwriting), the organization must identify, document, and maintain a specific Art. 9(2) legal basis in its Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) before processing commences. Pass condition: no special-category data processing activity exists without a recorded, approved Art. 9(2) condition.

title: Audit Logging of Special-Category Data Access and Processing
requirement: All access to, and processing of, special-category data (reads, writes, exports, and deletions) must be captured in tamper-evident audit logs retained for the period required by applicable law. Pass condition: automated log coverage is verified across all special-category data systems, with no gaps, and logs are available for review upon regulatory inquiry or internal audit.

title: Audit Rights Provision in Processor Contracts
requirement: All DPAs must include contractual audit-rights clauses entitling the insurer to conduct or commission audits of each processor's and sub-processor's data protection controls. Pass condition: every executed DPA contains enforceable audit-rights language and evidence of at least one rights-exercise or assessment per contract term.

title: Automated Audit-Ready Evidence Capture
requirement: Controls must be instrumented to capture audit evidence automatically wherever technically feasible, including system-generated logs, access records, and compliance telemetry. Pass condition: an audit of any privacy control yields automatically produced, tamper-evident evidence without reliance solely on manual attestation.

title: Automated deletion or anonymisation at end of retention
requirement: Automated technical controls must execute deletion or irreversible anonymisation of identifiable data records upon expiry of their assigned retention period, without manual intervention being required to trigger the process. Pass condition: automated jobs demonstrably fire at or before the retention end-date for every data category, with no identifiable records surviving beyond their scheduled expiry.

title: Consent withdrawal mechanism — equally easy as granting
requirement: The insurer must provide data subjects with a mechanism to withdraw consent at any time that is no more burdensome than the method used to grant consent (e.g., if consent was granted via a single click on a web form, withdrawal must also be achievable via a single click). Pass condition: withdrawal pathway is present in every channel where consent is collected, completes in the same or fewer steps as granting, and triggers immediate cessation of processing for the withdrawn purpose.

title: Contestation Right & Remediation Process for Automated Decisions
requirement: The insurer must provide data subjects with a clearly communicated, accessible mechanism to contest the outcome of an automated decision and must document the investigation and resolution of each contest, including any remediation applied. Pass condition: all contests are logged, responded to within the prescribed timeframe, and outcomes are tracked for quality review.

title: DPO Formal Designation & Independence Requirement
requirement: The organization must formally designate a Data Protection Officer who is adequately resourced and structurally independent (i.e., not subject to instructions regarding the exercise of DPO tasks, with no conflicts of interest). Pass condition: a documented appointment record exists, the DPO's position is free from conflicting duties, and sufficient budget/staff support is allocated.

title: DPO Involvement in All Personal-Data Matters
