requirement: The designated DPO must be systematically consulted and involved in all processes, projects, and decisions that involve the processing of personal data. Pass condition: documented evidence (e.g., project sign-off records, privacy impact assessment reviews) shows DPO participation across all relevant personal-data activities.

title: DPO as Data Subject Contact Point
requirement: The DPO must serve as the accessible contact point for data subjects exercising their rights (e.g., access, erasure, rectification) and addressing privacy inquiries. Pass condition: a published, functional mechanism routes data subject requests to the DPO and responses are managed within required timeframes.

title: DPO as Supervisory Authority Contact Point
requirement: The DPO must serve as the designated, publicly accessible contact point for the relevant data-protection supervisory authority on all matters relating to personal-data processing and compliance. Pass condition: regulator communications are routed to and handled by the DPO, and contact details are published/disclosed as required.

title: DSAR confirmation-of-processing response
requirement: Upon receipt of a Data Subject Access Request (DSAR), the insurer must confirm in writing whether or not the data subject's personal data is being processed, including the purposes, categories, and legal basis of that processing. The obligation is satisfied when every DSAR receives a documented confirmation-of-processing statement delivered to the data subject within one calendar month of the verified request.

title: DSAR data copy and processing metadata delivery
requirement: Upon a verified DSAR, the insurer must produce and transmit to the data subject a complete copy of all personal data held, together with associated processing metadata (retention periods, third-party recipients, data sources, and any automated decision-making logic). The obligation is satisfied when the complete data package plus metadata is delivered to the requestor within one calendar month of the verified request.

title: Data Collection Minimisation Enforcement
requirement: The organization must collect only personal data fields that are strictly necessary for the explicitly stated processing purpose. Pass condition: no data collection pipeline or intake form captures fields beyond those documented as necessary for the declared purpose.

title: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) Execution with Processors
requirement: Every processor and sub-processor engaged by the insurer must be bound by a written Art. 28-compliant Data Processing Agreement (DPA) before any personal data processing begins. Pass condition: 100% of active processors and sub-processors have a fully executed, current DPA on file that meets Art. 28 requirements.

title: Data Restore & Processing Resilience Capability
requirement: The insurer must establish and maintain a documented capability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner following a physical or technical incident, including tested backup-and-restore procedures and resilience architecture for all personal data processing systems. Pass condition: restore capability is documented, assigned an RTO/RPO, and evidence of a successful restore test exists within the past review cycle.

title: Design-Time Rejection of Purposeless Fields
requirement: Data architecture, system design, and engineering processes must incorporate a control that automatically or procedurally rejects the inclusion of any data field that lacks a documented purpose prior to deployment. Pass condition: no field without a documented purpose can be promoted to production; evidenced by design review sign-off and pipeline validation rules.

title: Direct controller-to-controller data transmission mechanism
requirement: Where technically feasible, the insurer must establish and operate a capability to transmit a data subject's provided personal data directly to another designated controller upon the subject's instruction. The obligation is met when a verified portability request citing a receiving controller results in a successful, secure, direct transmission to that controller without requiring the subject to act as an intermediary.

title: Documented Privacy Policy Suite
requirement: The organization must maintain a complete, current set of documented privacy policies covering every privacy control obligation. Pass condition: an auditor can retrieve a version-controlled policy document for each applicable privacy control, with approval records and effective dates.

title: EU AI Act High-Risk Obligation Crosswalk for Automated Decision Systems
requirement: The insurer must produce and maintain a documented crosswalk mapping each in-scope automated decision system (automated underwriting, pricing, claims triage) to the applicable EU AI Act high-risk AI obligations (conformity assessment, risk management, human oversight, data governance, transparency, and logging requirements). Pass condition: the crosswalk is completed, reviewed by legal and AI governance, and updated whenever a system is materially changed or a new high-risk system is introduced.
frequency: annual and event-driven on material change

title: Erasure from backups, caches, and logs
requirement: Upon verified erasure trigger, personal data must be purged or rendered irrecoverable from all backup systems, caches, and log repositories within a defined and documented retention schedule. Pass condition: backup/cache/log purge process is executed and evidenced for each valid erasure request, with no recoverable personal data remaining beyond the next scheduled purge cycle.

title: Erasure propagation to third-party processors
requirement: When a valid erasure request is fulfilled, the insurer must notify and confirm deletion with all downstream third-party data processors who hold or process the relevant personal data on its behalf. Pass condition: written confirmation of deletion is obtained from each processor within the required regulatory timeframe for every erasure event.

title: Heightened Safeguards Implementation for Special-Category Data
requirement: Technical and organizational safeguards beyond baseline data-protection controls (e.g., encryption at rest and in transit, pseudonymization, data minimization, and segregation of special-category data stores) must be designed, implemented, and maintained for all systems processing health, biometric, genetic, or other special-category data. Pass condition: a documented safeguard assessment confirms heightened controls are active for every special-category data store and processing pipeline.

title: High-Risk Breach Notification to Affected Data Subjects
requirement: Where a personal data breach is assessed as posing a high risk to the rights and freedoms of affected individuals, the insurer must notify those data subjects without undue delay. The pass condition is evidence of timely, individualized subject notifications for every high-risk breach, with no unjustified delay documented.

title: Human Review Mechanism for Automated Decisions
requirement: The insurer must establish and operationalize a process by which any individual subject to a solely automated decision with legal or similarly significant effects can request meaningful human review of that decision by a qualified employee with authority to override it. Pass condition: the human-review pathway is documented, tested, and completed within a defined SLA for each in-scope business line.

title: Instruction-Only Processing Obligation Enforcement
requirement: Processors must be contractually restricted to processing personal data solely on documented written instructions from the insurer, with any out-of-scope processing prohibited and tracked. Pass condition: DPAs include an instruction-only clause, and evidence of documented processing instructions exists for each active engagement with no record of unauthorised processing.

title: Lawful Basis Documentation per Processing Activity
requirement: Before any personal data is collected, each processing activity must have one documented Art. 6 lawful basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests) recorded in the organization's processing activity inventory. Pass condition: every active processing activity in the inventory carries a pre-collection lawful basis entry with no gaps.

title: Lawful Ground Establishment for Automated Decisions
requirement: For each automated processing activity that produces decisions with legal or similarly significant effects (e.g., automated underwriting, pricing, claims triage), the insurer must identify, document, and establish a valid lawful basis before deployment. Pass condition: every in-scope automated decision system has a recorded, approved lawful ground that is reviewed at least annually and upon material change.
frequency: annual and event-driven on material change

title: Legitimate-Interests Balancing Test Record
requirement: For every processing activity that relies on legitimate interests as its Art. 6 lawful basis, a documented balancing test must be completed and retained prior to data collection, demonstrating that the controller's interests are not overridden by the data subject's rights. Pass condition: no legitimate-interests basis is active without an accompanying, dated balancing test record stored in the processing activity inventory.

title: Machine-assisted DSAR fulfilment mechanism
requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain a machine-assisted (automated or tool-supported) workflow capable of locating, collating, and packaging a data subject's personal data and metadata across all in-scope systems to support timely DSAR responses. The obligation is satisfied when a documented, operational tooling solution demonstrably reduces manual effort and enables consistent completion of DSARs within the one-month statutory deadline.

title: Meaningful Logic Disclosure for Automated Decision Systems
requirement: For each automated decision system with legal or similarly significant effects, the insurer must produce and maintain consumer-facing disclosures that explain in plain language the logic, key inputs, and likely consequences of the automated processing. Pass condition: disclosures are accessible at or before the point of automated decision and are kept current with model changes.

title: Objection-to-processing flag enforcement at data layer
requirement: The organization must implement and maintain objection flags at the data layer such that, when a data subject objects to processing of their personal data under a legitimate-interest or public-task basis, the flag is applied immediately and respected by all downstream systems and jobs. The pass condition is that processing ceases for the objected purpose within the required response window and no downstream job overrides or ignores the flag.

title: Opt-in consent capture at point of collection
requirement: Where consent is the legal basis for processing personal data, the insurer must capture a freely-given, specific, informed, and unambiguous affirmative opt-in from the data subject before any processing occurs. Pass condition: no personal data is processed under a consent basis unless a documented, affirmative opt-in action (not pre-ticked box or silence) has been recorded for that specific purpose.

title: Per-Field Purpose Documentation Register
requirement: Every data field collected or stored must have a documented, approved business purpose recorded in a central data catalogue or register. Pass condition: 100% of active data fields map to at least one explicit, approved purpose statement with no undocumented fields present.

title: Per-data-category retention schedule documentation
requirement: The organization must maintain a documented, approved retention schedule that assigns a defined maximum retention period to each category of personal/identifiable data it holds. Pass condition: a current, comprehensive schedule exists covering all data categories, is reviewed at least annually, and is approved by the accountable owner.

title: Personal Data Accuracy Maintenance Mechanism
requirement: The organization must implement and operate ongoing controls and processes (e.g., data validation rules, periodic data quality reviews) that proactively keep personal data accurate and up-to-date across all systems of record. Pass condition: documented accuracy controls exist and evidence of regular data quality monitoring is maintained.

title: Personal Data Breach Detection & Assessment Process
requirement: The insurer must maintain an operational process to detect potential personal data breaches, triage them, and assess severity and notifiability. The pass condition is a documented, tested breach-detection-and-assessment workflow with defined roles, severity criteria, and evidence of execution for each incident.

title: Personal Data Breach Register
requirement: The insurer must maintain a breach register that records all personal data breaches, including their facts, effects, and remedial actions taken, regardless of whether notification was required. The pass condition is a current, complete register that is available for supervisory inspection at any time and is updated following every identified breach.

title: Personal Data Rectification Request Fulfillment Within One Month
requirement: Upon receipt of a data subject rectification request, the organization must correct inaccurate personal data across all relevant systems and confirm completion to the requestor within one calendar month. Pass condition: 100% of rectification requests are fulfilled and confirmed within 30 days of receipt, with a complete audit trail per request.

title: Pre-build DPIA completion & sign-off for high-risk processing
requirement: A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) must be fully completed and formally signed off by the accountable owner before any build or processing activity commences where the intended processing is deemed high-risk to data subjects. The pass condition is a documented, approved DPIA on record prior to the start of build, evidencing identified risks, mitigating controls, and residual risk determination.

title: Prior supervisory authority consultation where residual risk remains high
requirement: Where a completed DPIA concludes that residual risk remains high and cannot be sufficiently mitigated by internal controls, the organisation must conduct prior consultation with the relevant supervisory authority (per Art. 36 GDPR) before processing begins. The pass condition is documented evidence of the consultation submission to the supervisory authority and receipt of its response (or expiry of the consultation period) prior to commencement of the high-risk processing.

title: Privacy Accountability Audit Readiness Programme
requirement: The organization must operate a formal accountability programme that aggregates policies, decision records, and evidence artefacts into an audit-ready package and periodically verifies completeness. Pass condition: a regulator or internal auditor can request and receive a full evidence pack for any privacy control within a defined SLA, with no material gaps identified.

title: Privacy Decision Record Maintenance
requirement: For each material privacy decision (e.g., lawful-basis determinations, DPIA outcomes, consent scope changes), a structured decision record must be created and retained. Pass condition: every qualifying decision has a retrievable, dated record that identifies the decision-maker, rationale, and outcome.

title: Privacy Notice Delivery at or Before Data Collection
requirement: A plain-language, layered privacy notice meeting Art. 13/14 content requirements must be presented to every data subject at or before the point of personal data collection. Pass condition: no personal data is collected without the compliant notice having been surfaced to the data subject through the relevant channel.

title: Privacy-by-Default System Configuration
requirement: All systems must default to the most privacy-protective settings available at the point of deployment and release, ensuring that no more personal data is processed than is necessary for each specified purpose without affirmative action by the user or administrator. Pass condition: release acceptance criteria include a verified privacy-default configuration check, confirmed by the Data Protection Officer before go-live.

title: Privacy-by-Design Architecture Embedding
requirement: Privacy controls — including pseudonymisation, data minimisation, and access limits — must be embedded into system and solution architecture from the inception of any new or materially changed system. Pass condition: architecture review artifacts demonstrate that privacy controls are incorporated at design stage prior to build commencement, with documented sign-off from the Data Protection Officer.
frequency: per new or materially changed system design

title: Processing-restriction flag enforcement at data layer
requirement: The organization must implement and maintain processing-restriction flags at the data layer such that, when a data subject invokes their right to restriction of processing, the flag is applied immediately and durably in the authoritative data store. The pass condition is that no downstream system, batch job, or pipeline reads or acts on restricted records for prohibited purposes while the flag is active.

title: Prohibition on Incompatible Secondary Use of Data
requirement: Personal data collected for one stated purpose must not be re-used for any secondary purpose that is incompatible with the original collection purpose, unless a fresh legal basis and purpose statement is documented and approved. Pass condition: no downstream use case or analytics workload processes personal data outside its documented compatible purpose scope, verified through data lineage and privacy impact reviews.

title: Prohibition on indefinite storage of identifiable data
requirement: No personal or otherwise identifiable data may be retained without an assigned, finite retention period; any data store containing identifiable records must be governed by the approved retention schedule. Pass condition: data inventory confirms zero data stores classified as 'indefinite' or 'retain until further notice' for identifiable data, verified through periodic data governance audits.

title: Rectification/erasure notification to data recipients (Art. 19)
requirement: Where personal data has been disclosed to recipients (e.g., reinsurers, service providers, analytics partners), the insurer must communicate any rectification or erasure to each recipient and maintain a log of notifications. Pass condition: every rectification or erasure event generates a timestamped notification record sent to all identified recipients, with acknowledgements retained.

title: Regular Effectiveness Testing of Security-of-Processing Controls
requirement: The insurer must conduct regular, scheduled testing of the effectiveness of all technical and organisational measures applied to personal data processing (including encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality, integrity, availability, and resilience controls), with results documented and remediation actions tracked. Pass condition: a testing schedule exists, test results are recorded at the required cadence, and findings are closed within defined SLAs.

title: Restrictive Access Controls for Special-Category Data
requirement: Access to health, biometric, genetic, and other special-category data must be restricted to only those roles with a documented business need, enforced through role-based access controls (RBAC) with approval workflows. Pass condition: quarterly access reviews demonstrate that no user or system account holds access to special-category data without a current, approved justification.

title: Risk-Appropriate Technical & Organisational Measures Implementation
requirement: The insurer must implement and maintain a documented suite of risk-appropriate technical and organisational measures — including encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality controls, integrity controls, availability controls, and resilience mechanisms — applied across all personal data processing systems. Pass condition: a current, approved controls inventory exists mapping each measure to identified processing risks, aligned to the Encryption and Application Security standards.

title: RoPA inventory creation and maintenance
requirement: The organization must maintain a living Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) inventory that documents, for each processing activity, the purpose of processing, categories of personal data, recipients, cross-border transfers, and retention periods. The inventory is considered compliant when it is complete, accurate, and accessible at all times as a living document.

title: RoPA update upon system or process change
requirement: Whenever a new system is introduced, an existing system is materially changed, or a processing activity is added, modified, or retired, the RoPA must be updated to reflect the change before or at the point of go-live. The pass condition is that no active processing activity exists without a current, accurate RoPA entry.

title: Served Notice Version Record Against Data Subject
requirement: The exact version of the privacy notice served to each data subject must be recorded and linked to that individual's record at the time of collection, creating a durable audit trail. Pass condition: a retrievable log exists showing which notice version was presented to which data subject and when, with no gaps for any collection event.

title: Structured machine-readable data export capability
requirement: The insurer must produce and maintain a mechanism that exports a data subject's provided personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format (e.g., JSON or CSV) upon request. The obligation is met when any verified data subject request results in a complete, well-formed export delivered in at least one machine-readable format within the required response window.

title: Sub-Processor Authorisation Chain Documentation
requirement: A documented authorisation chain must be maintained for every sub-processor, recording the insurer's prior written approval (general or specific) and each link from controller to processor to sub-processor. Pass condition: a complete, up-to-date register exists showing the authorisation lineage for every sub-processor in use.

title: Supplementary Measures Implementation
requirement: Where a TIA identifies that the transfer mechanism alone does not ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection, the insurer must identify, implement, and document supplementary technical and/or organisational measures (e.g., encryption, pseudonymisation, contractual restrictions) before the transfer commences or continues. Pass condition: documented supplementary measures are in place and operational for every transfer where the TIA found a residual protection gap.
frequency: per transfer with identified protection gap

title: Timestamped consent record with notice version
requirement: For every consent collected, the insurer must store a durable consent record that captures the data subject identity, the specific purpose consented to, the exact timestamp of consent, and the version of the privacy notice presented at the time of collection. Pass condition: audit of any consent event can produce a complete, retrievable record containing all four elements within a reasonable retrieval window.

title: Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) Execution
requirement: Prior to each EEA personal data transfer, or upon material change in destination-country law or processing context, the insurer must complete and document a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) evaluating the legal landscape and practical risks of the destination country (post-Schrems II). Pass condition: a completed, signed TIA exists for every active EEA data transfer relationship and is refreshed when circumstances change.
frequency: per new or materially changed transfer

title: Valid Transfer Mechanism Maintenance
requirement: For every flow of personal data out of the EEA, the insurer must have a valid, documented legal transfer mechanism in place—adequacy decision, Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), or Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs)—before the transfer occurs. Pass condition: every identified EEA-to-third-country data flow is covered by a current, executed transfer mechanism with no gaps.

title: Verified deletion across all primary data stores
requirement: When erasure conditions are met (per applicable regulation), the insurer must verifiably delete the data subject's personal data from all primary operational data stores, databases, and repositories. Pass condition: documented proof of deletion from each primary store exists for every valid erasure request.

title: Customer-specific suitability determination for securities recommendations
requirement: Before making any securities or strategy recommendation to a specific customer, the firm must assess and document that the recommendation is suitable for that individual customer based on their investment profile (risk tolerance, financial situation, investment objectives, time horizon, liquidity needs). Pass condition: a per-customer suitability record exists and is retained for every recommendation made.

title: Deferred Variable Annuity Exchange Surveillance Program
requirement: The member must implement and maintain a supervisory surveillance program specifically designed to detect, review, and document potentially unsuitable deferred variable annuity exchanges (1035 exchanges and internal replacements). The obligation is met when the program produces documented surveillance reviews with disposition records for all identified exchange activity on a continuous basis.

title: Deferred Variable Annuity Pre-Sale Disclosure Package
requirement: At or before the time of each deferred variable annuity transaction, the member must provide the customer with clear written disclosure of all surrender charges, fees, tax implications, and material risks associated with the product. The obligation is met when documented disclosure is delivered and acknowledged by the customer prior to or at the point of sale.

title: Deferred Variable Annuity Representative Training Program
requirement: The member must establish and maintain a formal training program ensuring that all registered representatives who recommend deferred variable annuities are trained on the product's features, risks, suitability standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. The obligation is met when training completion records exist for all in-scope representatives and the curriculum is reviewed and updated at least annually.

title: Designated supervisory principals assignment
requirement: The firm must designate qualified registered principals responsible for supervising each type of business activity in which the firm engages. Pass condition: every material business activity has a named, appropriately registered principal of record with documented supervisory accountability.

title: FINRA filing of retail communications
requirement: Certain categories of retail communications must be filed with FINRA (within prescribed timelines, e.g., within 10 business days of first use, or pre-use for new members). Pass condition: all required retail communications are filed with FINRA on time and an evidenced filing log is maintained.

title: Fair, balanced and non-misleading communications standard
requirement: All public communications (retail, correspondence, and institutional) must be fair, balanced, and not misleading in content, including accurate representations of risks and benefits. Pass condition: periodic review confirms no communications contain false, exaggerated, or omitted material information that could mislead a recipient.

title: Member-as-Principal-Underwriter Requirements for Variable Contracts
requirement: Where the member acts as principal underwriter for variable contracts of an insurance company, it must satisfy all FINRA Rule 2320 requirements applicable to that capacity, including maintenance of required agreements, disclosures, and supervisory controls. Pass condition: written agreements in place, supervisory procedures documented, and annual review evidencing compliance with principal-underwriter obligations.

title: Principal Review & Approval of Deferred Variable Annuity Applications Within 7 Business Days
requirement: A registered principal must review and either approve or reject each completed deferred variable annuity application within 7 business days of receipt. The obligation is met when a documented principal sign-off timestamp is recorded within the 7-business-day window for every application submitted.

title: Principal pre-approval of retail communications
requirement: A registered principal must review and approve each retail communication before first use or filing. Pass condition: documented approval records exist for every retail communication prior to its dissemination, signed or logged by an eligible principal.

title: Quantitative suitability review for recommended series of transactions
requirement: The firm must monitor and review recommended series or patterns of transactions for a customer account to ensure the aggregate activity is not excessive (churning/over-trading) relative to the customer's investment profile. Pass condition: periodic quantitative review reports are produced identifying accounts where recommended transaction volume or turnover may be unsuitable, with escalation records where triggered.

title: Reasonable-basis suitability analysis for recommended securities/strategies
requirement: The firm must conduct and document a reasonable-basis suitability analysis establishing that a recommended security or investment strategy has a plausible basis for suitability for at least some investors, based on adequate due diligence. Pass condition: documented product/strategy-level due diligence exists prior to any recommendation being made to customers.

title: Review of associated persons' business activities
requirement: Designated principals must conduct and document regular reviews of the business activities of each associated person under their supervision to detect and prevent regulatory violations. Pass condition: evidence of periodic documented review (e.g., trade reviews, activity logs) exists for each supervised person.

title: Review of associated persons' communications
requirement: The firm must review correspondence and communications (written, electronic, and social media) of associated persons in accordance with the WSPs to ensure compliance with applicable rules. Pass condition: a documented communications review process exists with records of reviews performed and supervisory sign-offs.

title: Securities-distribution applicability gate — registered products
requirement: The insurer must formally document and maintain a written determination identifying which products (variable annuities, variable life, RILAs, mutual funds, 529s) are distributed through an affiliated or third-party broker-dealer and therefore subject to FINRA, SEC, and MSRB requirements, while explicitly excluding fixed annuities and traditional life from that perimeter. Pass condition: a current, approved applicability matrix or scope document exists, is reviewed at least annually (and upon any product launch or distribution-channel change), and is accessible to compliance, legal, and product teams.

title: Supervisory review & handling of customer complaints
requirement: The firm must implement a supervisory process for the receipt, review, and resolution of customer complaints, including escalation to a registered principal. Pass condition: all complaints are logged, reviewed by a designated principal, and addressed in accordance with WSPs, with documented disposition records.

title: Supervisory system design & implementation
requirement: The firm must establish and maintain a supervisory system — including defined reporting lines, supervisory assignments, and controls — reasonably designed to ensure associated persons comply with applicable securities laws and FINRA rules. Pass condition: a documented supervisory system exists with clear role assignments and operational controls evidencing active supervision.

title: Variable Contract Payment Receipt & Transmittal Obligation
requirement: The member firm must promptly receive and transmit all customer payments for variable contracts to the issuing insurance company in accordance with FINRA Rule 2320. Pass condition: documented evidence of timely transmittal (within required timeframes) for each payment received, with no un-transmitted funds held beyond the permitted period.

title: Variable Contract Sales-Charge Limits Compliance
requirement: The member firm must ensure that sales charges imposed on variable contract sales do not exceed the maximum permissible limits prescribed by FINRA Rule 2320. Pass condition: all sales-charge schedules and actual charges collected are reviewed and confirmed to be at or below the regulatory cap on a per-contract and aggregate basis.

title: Written Supervisory Procedures (WSPs) establishment & maintenance
requirement: The firm must establish, maintain, and enforce written supervisory procedures (WSPs) that are reasonably designed to achieve compliance with applicable securities laws and FINRA rules. Pass condition: WSPs are documented, current, accessible to relevant personnel, and cover all required business activities.

title: Real-time DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer must maintain a live electronic interface enabling Florida DMV and state verification systems to query individual policy coverage status in real time, with accurate, up-to-date responses returned within the timeframe mandated by the program. Pass condition: the query endpoint is operational, policy data returned matches current policy administration records, and response SLAs are consistently met.

title: Recurring policy data feed to Florida motor vehicle insurance verification program
requirement: The insurer must maintain and operate automated, recurring electronic data feeds from its policy administration systems to Florida's motor vehicle insurance verification program, supplying current auto policy information (insured, vehicle, coverage dates) on the required submission schedule. Pass condition: feeds are delivered on time, in the prescribed format, and without material gaps or rejections.

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its complete annual financial statement to the Florida regulator through the NAIC iSite+ centralized repository on an annual basis. The obligation is satisfied when the filing is accepted and distributed to the Florida Department of Financial Services / OIR via the NAIC system within the statutory deadline.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Change Filing via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file and maintain its Florida Certificate of Authority and submit all material corporate changes (e.g., name changes, mergers, new lines of authority) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). Pass condition: a current, valid Florida COA is on file and all corporate changes are submitted via UCAA within required timeframes.
frequency: per corporate change or renewal event

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment Maintenance via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit, renew, and maintain all Florida producer/agent licenses and company appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). Pass condition: all active producers writing Florida business hold a current, NIPR-filed license and appointment with no lapses.
frequency: continuous; renewal per license expiration cycle

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the Florida regulator through the NAIC iSite+ centralized repository on an annual basis. The obligation is satisfied when the MCAS data is accepted by iSite+ and distributed to Florida regulators, with all required lines of business and data elements accurately reported.

title: Florida IRFS Electronic Filing Submission
requirement: The insurer must submit all rate, rule, and form filings for Florida through the state's proprietary Insurance Rate Filing System (IRFS) rather than SERFF. A filing is compliant only when all required electronic filing components are successfully uploaded and accepted by the Florida IRFS portal.

title: IRFS-Compatible Filing Component Production
requirement: The insurer's product and rate systems must be configured to produce all electronic filing components (e.g., structured data, forms, rate/rule exhibits) in the formats and specifications required by the Florida IRFS portal. Pass condition: all generated outputs meet IRFS technical specifications and can be submitted without manual reformatting.

title: Separate Florida direct filing for Compact-eligible annuity products
requirement: Because Florida is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, annuity products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the Florida OIR. The obligation is met when a stand-alone Florida product filing is submitted and approved by the OIR prior to sale or issuance in the state.

title: Separate Florida direct filing for Compact-eligible disability products
requirement: Because Florida is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, disability income and income-protection products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the Florida OIR. The obligation is met when a stand-alone Florida disability product filing is submitted and approved by the OIR prior to sale in the state.

title: Separate Florida direct filing for Compact-eligible life products
requirement: Because Florida is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, life insurance products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation (OIR). The obligation is met when a stand-alone Florida product filing is submitted and approved by the OIR prior to sale in the state.

title: Separate Florida direct filing for Compact-eligible long-term care products
requirement: Because Florida is not a member of the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact, long-term care (LTC) products that would qualify for Compact filing in other states must be filed directly and separately with the Florida OIR. The obligation is met when a stand-alone Florida LTC product filing is submitted and approved by the OIR prior to sale in the state.

title: FROI/SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying Florida workers' compensation claim, the insurer must submit First Reports of Injury (FROI) and Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) electronically to the Florida regulator using IAIABC EDI transaction sets within the prescribed statutory timeframes. Pass condition: all reportable claims have a corresponding outbound EDI transmission logged with correct transaction type, content, and submission timestamp.

title: IAIABC EDI Acknowledgment Receipt & Error Resolution
requirement: The insurer must capture, retain, and act upon all EDI acknowledgment transactions (e.g., TA1, 999, and regulator-level acknowledgments) returned by the Florida regulator for each FROI/SROI submission, resolving any rejected or errored transactions within required timeframes. Pass condition: acknowledgment records are stored for each transmission, error rates are tracked, and rejected transactions are corrected and resubmitted with documented resolution evidence.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the Florida workers' compensation regulator (DFS/OJCC) under IAIABC EDI standards before any FROI/SROI transmissions are sent. Pass condition: a valid, current trading-partner agreement/registration record is on file with the regulator and internally documented.

title: Georgia DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer's policy administration systems must be capable of responding to real-time or batch verification queries initiated by the Georgia DMV or state verification program, returning accurate coverage status for the queried vehicle/policy. Pass condition: all inbound state/DMV queries receive a valid, timely response with correct coverage data.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Georgia motor vehicle insurance verification data feed
requirement: The insurer's policy administration systems must continuously provide recurring policy data feeds to Georgia's motor vehicle insurance verification program, ensuring active and lapsed auto policy data is transmitted to the state/DMV on an ongoing basis. Pass condition: scheduled data feeds are delivered accurately and on time without gaps or rejections by the state system.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to the Georgia Insurance Commissioner through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository, which then distributes the filing to the state regulator. The obligation is met when the complete annual statement is successfully lodged in iSite+ by the statutory deadline and confirmed as received by the NAIC system.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Changes via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file all Georgia company Certificate of Authority applications and any material corporate changes (e.g., name, ownership, lines of business) through the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). Pass condition: the insurer holds a current Georgia Certificate of Authority for all written lines, with all corporate changes timely filed and approved via UCAA before taking effect.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit, renew, and maintain all Georgia producer/agent licenses and company appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). Pass condition: all active Georgia producers and agents hold current, NIPR-filed licenses and appointments with no lapsed or unauthorized placements.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the Georgia Insurance Commissioner through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository for distribution to the state regulator. The obligation is met when MCAS data is accurately completed, successfully uploaded to iSite+, and confirmed as accepted by the NAIC system within the prescribed filing period.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Electronic premium tax payment submission via OPTins
requirement: The insurer must remit Georgia premium tax payments electronically through the NAIC OPTins system. The obligation is satisfied when each required premium tax payment is transmitted and accepted via OPTins by the applicable due date.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: IIPRC Compact eligibility determination for life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: Before filing, the insurer must assess each life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability product to determine whether it qualifies for the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) filing path under Georgia's membership. The pass condition is a documented eligibility determination on file for each product prior to submission.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: IIPRC approved product implementation across member states
requirement: Upon Compact approval of a filed product, the insurer must implement the approved form and rates uniformly across all IIPRC member states, including Georgia, without re-filing at the individual state level. The pass condition is documented evidence that the approved product version is deployed in all applicable member-state markets consistent with the Compact approval order.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: IIPRC uniform product filing submission via SERFF portal
requirement: For each eligible life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product, the insurer must submit a single uniform filing through the IIPRC's SERFF portal, covering all Compact member states including Georgia, in lieu of individual state filings. The pass condition is a confirmed SERFF submission with an assigned IIPRC filing number and acknowledgment of receipt from the Compact.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: SERFF Electronic Submission of Rate, Rule, and Form Filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Georgia must be submitted electronically via NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF and accepted by the Georgia Department of Insurance before the product goes live.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: SERFF Filing Evidence Preservation (Receipt ID, Status, Submission Date)
requirement: For every Georgia rate, rule, and form filing submitted via SERFF, the insurer must preserve the filing evidence — including the SERFF receipt ID, filing status, and submission date — before implementing the associated product. The pass condition is that a complete, retrievable record of this evidence exists in the insurer's records management system at the time of product launch.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Surplus lines tax filing submission via OPTins
requirement: Where required by Georgia, the insurer must submit surplus lines tax filings electronically through the NAIC OPTins system. The obligation is satisfied when each surplus lines tax filing is successfully transmitted and accepted via OPTins within the state-mandated filing period.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)
frequency: per surplus lines tax filing cycle

title: FROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: The insurer must electronically submit First Reports of Injury (FROI) to the Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation using IAIABC EDI standards within the state-mandated filing deadline for each qualifying lost-time or medical-only claim. Pass condition: timely, well-formed FROI transactions accepted by the trading-partner gateway with no fatal errors.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: FROI/SROI EDI Acknowledgment Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture and retain electronic acknowledgment records (999/TA1 and regulator-level acknowledgment transactions) for every FROI and SROI transmission as evidence of successful or failed delivery. Pass condition: acknowledgment evidence is stored, reconciled against submitted transactions, and retrievable for regulatory audit or examination.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must register as an approved IAIABC EDI trading partner with the Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation prior to transmitting FROI/SROI transactions. Pass condition: a current, active trading-partner agreement/registration on file with the regulator.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: The insurer must electronically submit Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the Georgia State Board of Workers' Compensation using IAIABC EDI standards whenever a reportable change in claim status occurs (e.g., return-to-work, benefit change, closure). Pass condition: timely, well-formed SROI transactions accepted by the trading-partner gateway with no fatal errors.
citation: Title 33 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated (O.C.G.A.)

title: Hawaii APCD recurring claims data extract submission
requirement: Health insurers must compile and submit recurring claims data extracts to Hawaii's all-payer claims database (APCD) in accordance with the state's APCD submission guide, including required data elements, file formats, and submission cadence. The obligation is satisfied when complete, conformant extracts are delivered to the APCD on schedule per the submission guide.
frequency: recurring (per Hawaii APCD submission guide schedule)

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to Hawaii's state regulator through NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when the complete annual statement is successfully filed in iSite+ and distributed to the Hawaii Insurance Division within the required statutory deadline.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Change Filing via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file and maintain its Hawaii Certificate of Authority, and submit any corporate changes (e.g., mergers, name changes, lines of business additions), through the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is satisfied when all company-level licensing actions and material corporate changes in Hawaii are processed via the UCAA and a valid Certificate of Authority remains in force.
frequency: per licensing action or corporate change

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment Maintenance via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must ensure all Hawaii producers/agents are licensed, renewed, and appointed through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR), maintaining current and accurate licensing records for each individual. The obligation is satisfied when no producer/agent transacts insurance business in Hawaii without a valid, NIPR-processed license and active appointment on file.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to Hawaii's state regulator through NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when all required MCAS data elements are accurately filed in iSite+ and distributed to the Hawaii Insurance Division within the required deadline.

title: Electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings via SERFF
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Hawaii must be submitted electronically through NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted via SERFF with a valid submission package (rate, rule, and/or form components as applicable) accepted by the Hawaii Insurance Division.

title: IIPRC Compact Filing Submission for Eligible Products
requirement: For eligible life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability products intended for Hawaii and other IIPRC member states, the insurer must file product forms once through the Compact's SERFF portal rather than submitting separate state-by-state filings. Pass condition: all eligible product types are filed via the IIPRC SERFF portal and approved under Compact standards prior to sale in member states.

title: IIPRC Member-State Coverage Maintenance
requirement: The insurer must continuously monitor Hawaii's and other relevant states' membership status in the IIPRC to ensure Compact filings remain effective for all targeted jurisdictions. Pass condition: an up-to-date record of active IIPRC member states is maintained, and any changes in membership are reflected in the insurer's filing strategy within 30 days of notification.

title: IIPRC Product Eligibility Determination
requirement: Prior to initiating any Compact filing, the insurer must assess each life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product to confirm it meets IIPRC eligibility criteria (product type, form standards, and state applicability). Pass condition: a documented eligibility determination exists for each product before a Compact filing is submitted.

title: Preservation of SERFF filing evidence prior to product implementation
requirement: For every Hawaii SERFF filing, the insurer must capture and retain the filing receipt ID, filing status, and submission date before any associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that these three data points are documented and retrievable in the filing record for each submission.

title: Hawaii Non-EDI Workers' Compensation Claim Reporting
requirement: The insurer must submit workers' compensation claim reports to Hawaii using the state-prescribed Non-EDI reporting channel and format, as required by the Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations. Reports must be submitted in compliance with the specific format, timing, and submission method mandated by Hawaii, with no EDI transmission used; pass condition is timely, complete, and correctly formatted claim reports delivered via the approved Non-EDI channel for all covered Hawaii workers' compensation claims.

title: Real-time DMV verification query response capability
requirement: The insurer must configure its policy administration systems to receive and respond to ad-hoc electronic insurance verification queries from the Idaho DMV or state verification system, returning accurate policy status in real time. Pass condition: all incoming state/DMV queries receive a timely, accurate electronic response with no unresolved or unanswered queries.

title: Recurring policy data feed to Idaho motor vehicle insurance verification program
requirement: The insurer must establish and maintain automated, recurring electronic data feeds from its policy administration systems to Idaho's motor vehicle insurance verification program, supplying current auto policy data on an ongoing basis. Pass condition: feeds are transmitted at the required cadence with no material gaps or failures in policy coverage data delivery.

title: Annual Financial Statement Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to the Idaho Department of Insurance through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository each year. The obligation is met when the complete annual statement is successfully filed in iSite+ and confirmed as distributed to the Idaho regulator within the required deadline.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Change Filings via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must obtain and maintain its Idaho Certificate of Authority, and submit any corporate changes (e.g., name change, state additions, amendments) through the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is met when the company's Idaho Certificate of Authority is current and all material corporate changes are filed and approved via UCAA prior to taking effect.
frequency: event-driven for corporate changes; annual renewal as required

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment Maintenance via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit, renew, and maintain all Idaho producer/agent licenses and company appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is met when every active producer writing Idaho business holds a current, NIPR-processed license and appointment on file with no lapses.
frequency: continuous; renewal per license expiration cycle

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the Idaho Department of Insurance through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository each year. The obligation is met when the MCAS data file is successfully filed in iSite+, validated, and confirmed as distributed to the Idaho regulator within the required deadline.

title: Electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings via SERFF
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Idaho must be submitted electronically through the NAIC SERFF system prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing has been transmitted through SERFF and is in an accepted or approved status before the product is deployed.

title: IIPRC uniform product filing via SERFF Compact portal
requirement: Eligible life insurance, annuity, LTC, and disability products must be filed once through the IIPRC's SERFF portal to obtain approval covering all member states, including Idaho, rather than submitting separate state-by-state filings. The obligation is satisfied when the SERFF Compact submission is complete, all required IIPRC standards documents are attached, and a filing receipt/tracking number is obtained from the Compact portal.

title: IIPRC-pathway eligibility determination for life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: Before filing a new life insurance, annuity, LTC, or disability product in Idaho (or other member states), the insurer must assess whether the product qualifies for the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) filing pathway rather than individual state filing. A product is deemed compliant when a documented eligibility determination — confirming the product type and state membership — is completed and retained prior to submission.

title: Preservation of SERFF filing evidence prior to product implementation
requirement: For each Idaho SERFF filing, the insurer must retain and preserve the filing receipt ID, submission date, and current filing status before any associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that these three data elements are recorded and retrievable in the filing records system for every rate, rule, and form submission.

title: FROI/SROI Acknowledgment Evidence Retention
requirement: The insurer must capture, store, and be able to produce evidence of electronic acknowledgments (e.g., 999/TA1 or equivalent IAIABC EDI acknowledgment records) returned by the Idaho regulator for each FROI/SROI transmission. Pass condition: a complete, auditable log of transmission acknowledgments is maintained and retrievable for every filed FROI/SROI transaction.

title: FROI/SROI Electronic Transmission via IAIABC EDI
requirement: For every qualifying Idaho workers' compensation claim, the insurer must electronically transmit First Reports of Injury (FROI) and Subsequent Reports of Injury (SROI) to the Idaho regulator using IAIABC EDI-compliant transaction sets within the mandated filing timeframes. Pass condition: all required FROI/SROI transactions are submitted on time, in valid IAIABC EDI format, for each covered claim.

title: IAIABC EDI Trading-Partner Registration
requirement: The insurer must complete and maintain active trading-partner registration with the Idaho workers' compensation regulator under IAIABC EDI standards before any FROI/SROI transmissions are made. Pass condition: a current, approved trading-partner agreement/registration record is on file with the Idaho regulator and internally documented.

title: Annual Financial Statement submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement (statutory annual statement) to the Illinois Department of Insurance through NAIC's centralized iSite+ repository, which distributes the filing to the state regulator. Pass condition: a complete, timely annual financial statement is accepted by iSite+ and confirmed as received by the Illinois regulator.

title: Insurer Company Licensing via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file and maintain its Illinois Certificate of Authority, and submit all corporate changes (e.g., name changes, line-of-business additions, mergers), using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is satisfied when the insurer's UCAA filings are current, approved, and reflect the company's authorized state of domicile and all lines written in Illinois.

title: Producer/Agent Licensing & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit, renew, and maintain all Illinois producer/agent licenses and company appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is satisfied when every active producer transacting business in Illinois holds a current, NIPR-filed license and appointment with no lapses.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to the Illinois Department of Insurance through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository. Pass condition: a complete and accurate MCAS filing is accepted by iSite+ and confirmed as distributed to the Illinois regulator within the prescribed annual deadline.

title: IIPRC eligibility determination for life/annuity/LTC/disability products
requirement: For each new or revised life insurance, annuity, long-term care, or disability product intended for Illinois and other member states, the insurer must formally assess whether the product qualifies for filing under the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Compact (IIPRC) rather than individual state filing. The pass condition is a documented eligibility determination—including the IIPRC product standard applied—completed before any filing path is selected.
frequency: per product development or revision cycle

title: IIPRC single-filing submission via SERFF for eligible products
requirement: For each product determined to be eligible under IIPRC standards, the insurer must submit the filing once through the Compact's SERFF portal, covering all member states including Illinois, in lieu of separate individual-state filings. The pass condition is a complete, accepted SERFF filing under the IIPRC filing track with a confirmed Compact receipt/acknowledgment for all targeted member states.

title: IIPRC-filed product compliance tracking and recordkeeping
requirement: The insurer must maintain a current register of all products filed and approved through the IIPRC Compact, recording the SERFF submission ID, approval date, applicable member states, and any post-approval amendments or withdrawals. The pass condition is an auditable record available on demand that maps each Compact-approved product to its active states and filing history.

title: Preservation of SERFF filing evidence prior to product implementation
requirement: For every Illinois SERFF filing, the insurer must retain the SERFF receipt ID, filing status, and submission date as documentary evidence before any associated product is implemented. The pass condition is that these three data points are captured and stored in a retrievable record for each filing prior to go-live.

title: SERFF electronic submission of rate, rule, and form filings
requirement: All rate, rule, and form filings for Illinois must be submitted electronically via NAIC SERFF prior to product implementation. The pass condition is that each filing is transmitted through SERFF with a valid submission date recorded before the product goes live.

title: Illinois Workers' Comp Claim Submission in Compliant Format
requirement: The insurer must submit workers' compensation claim data to Illinois authorities using the reporting channel and format determined to be currently required by the state. The pass condition is timely, accepted submission of WC claim reports in the validated Illinois-specific format with no regulatory rejection or deficiency notice.

title: Illinois Workers' Comp Reporting Channel & Format Review
requirement: The insurer must conduct and document a state-specific review of Illinois's current workers' compensation claim reporting channel and format requirements, given the state's mixed/evolving approach. The pass condition is a documented, up-to-date assessment confirming the correct submission channel and format in use for Illinois WC claim reports.

title: Annual Financial Statement Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must prepare and submit its annual financial statement to the Indiana Department of Insurance through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository each year. The obligation is met when the complete annual statement is successfully lodged in iSite+ within the required filing deadline and distributed to the state regulator.

title: Insurer Company Licensing & Corporate Changes via UCAA
requirement: The insurer must file all Indiana certificate-of-authority applications and material corporate changes (e.g., name change, state expansion, merger) using the NAIC Uniform Certificate of Authority Application (UCAA). The obligation is met when every active Indiana company license and any approved corporate change is supported by a completed, accepted UCAA filing.
frequency: per licensing event or corporate change

title: Producer/Agent Licensing, Renewal & Appointment via NIPR
requirement: The insurer must submit and maintain all Indiana producer/agent license applications, renewals, and appointments through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). The obligation is met when every active Indiana producer appointment is current, in good standing, and traceable to a completed NIPR transaction.

title: Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) Data Submission via NAIC iSite+
requirement: The insurer must compile and submit Market Conduct Annual Statement (MCAS) data to Indiana through NAIC's iSite+ centralized repository on an annual basis. The obligation is met when all required MCAS data elements are accurately filed in iSite+ within the prescribed deadline and made available to the Indiana regulator.

title: IIPRC approval maintenance and member-state compliance tracking
requirement: Once an IIPRC approval is granted, the insurer must continuously track the approved filing's status across all member states (including Indiana), maintain records of the Compact approval, and ensure the product form in use matches the approved IIPRC filing at all times. Pass condition: a current log of IIPRC-approved products with their approval dates, applicable member-state coverage, and any post-approval amendments is maintained and reconciled at each product refresh cycle.
